claims.statement: The Ministry's current list shows 17 legal online betting operators and a state monopoly for online casino and number games.

Polish law requires each online gambling operator to implement a regulator-approved responsible-gambling policy with age verification, registration, activity-control mechanisms, and loss-of-funds controls.
STS currently offers a three-month self-exclusion applied to its own account, evidencing an operator-level workaround rather than national portability.
The European Commission recommendation encourages national self-exclusion registries and operator consultation of them.
GAMSTOP and Sweden's Spelpaus demonstrate multi-operator exclusion checks at registration or login, but both obtain coverage through licensing or statutory requirements.
GDPR consent must be freely given, specific, informed, and withdrawable; profiling or solely automated decisions can add safeguards, so consent-only governance requires specialist analysis.
The foreign comparators imply that regulator-backed coverage, not an optional private consortium, is the critical structural requirement.

contrary_evidence: The reviewed Polish statute specifies operator-level responsible-gambling controls but does not establish the proposed shared registry.
STS already supplies a single-operator self-exclusion, so buyers can claim baseline compliance without a new network.
GAMSTOP and Spelpaus are mandated schemes; they do not validate voluntary Polish operator adoption.
Consent validity, withdrawal, identity matching, joint-controller roles, and automated access denial create unresolved GDPR design questions.
Only 17 licensed betting operators are listed, concentrating revenue and buyer power.

economics.acquisition_route: Hypothesis only: targeted subcontracting proposals to sponsor-appointed public-sector, identity, or gambling-compliance primes and independent controllers; no partner, sponsor, tender access, or channel commitment is evidenced
economics.capital_required_pln: Unknown; only a bounded reusable sandbox and scoped legal and security discovery are permitted before customer funding, while production capital must be covered by contracted milestones
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Unknown. Reuse across authorized deployments could expand beyond Poland's 17 private betting operators, but there is no evidenced buyer, outsourcing decision, price, win rate, margin, retention, or timing; no evidence-backed path to 5m PLN can be stated
economics.founder_time: Hypothesis: the founder handles technical architecture and data operations part-time while the customer or prime owns coalition work, public affairs, and governance; coordination, procurement support, and production on-call burden remain unknown and must be bounded before acceptance
economics.gross_margin_basis: Unknown. A reusable core and adapters could reduce marginal engineering, but the prime-contractor share, security, identity resolution, audits, insurance, uptime, incident response, and support are uncosted
economics.payback: Unknown. The structure forbids a production build until a paid milestone covers scoped work, reducing speculative cash exposure, but no paid engagement or sales-cycle evidence exists
economics.pricing: Hypothesis only: paid scoped technical discovery, then customer-funded implementation and acceptance milestones and a recurring white-label operations fee after lawful launch; no amount, willingness to pay, or conversion is evidenced
economics.retention_or_repeat: Evidence supports recurrent mandated checks in Britain and Sweden; hypothesis: a selected supplier could earn recurring operations fees while its customer retains the authorized role, but supplier retention and Polish demand are unproven

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Reusable jurisdiction rules engine, operator adapter library, audit and incident tooling, non-personal reliability learnings, and operating history embedded across sponsor-appointed deployments; public authority remains customer-owned
fingerprint.customer: Sponsor-appointed independent self-exclusion controllers and regulated-market prime contractors that hold, or are bidding for, authority to deploy a multi-operator scheme
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Targeted subcontracting proposals into sponsor-led procurements through established public-sector, identity, or gambling-compliance primes; no production build before paid discovery and verified customer authority; no channel relationship is currently evidenced
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Jurisdiction-configurable white-label status engine, minimal yes/no API, operator adapter kit, audit and appeals tooling, and contracted technical operations; the customer, not the founder company, owns lawful basis, scheme rules, mandate, and operator commitments; excludes wagering operations, raw betting histories, and automated addiction scoring
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The appointed controller or prime contractor pays for scoped technical discovery and, only after lawful authorization and binding participant commitments, implementation acceptance and recurring white-label operations; every price and paid conversion remains unvalidated
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A player requests broad self-exclusion or attempts to register or log in with a participating licensed operator during an active exclusion

founder_fit: Uses the founder's data engineering, privacy-preserving architecture, and AI-assisted product skills while avoiding operation of gambling
Places public affairs, scheme governance, lawful-basis ownership, and operator coalition work with the appointed controller or prime contractor rather than the founder
A paid-gate structure limits speculative production spending and concentrates founder work on a reusable technical module
Part-time technical discovery may fit the founder, but procurement support, specialist coordination, and production on-call burden are unknown and must be bounded before accepting work

redesign.economic_effect: Evidence: the reviewed foreign schemes show recurrent cross-operator checks where public authority compels participation, while the reviewed Polish material shows 17 listed private betting operators, operator-level controls, and no shared mandate. Hypothesis: selling a reusable white-label module to an appointed controller or prime, and gating production on a paid scoped milestone plus verified customer authority and participant commitments, transfers coalition and mandate-building work away from the founder, reduces speculative pre-revenue capital, and permits technical reuse beyond Poland. Unknown: no buyer, sponsor, prime relationship, outsourcing decision, payment, price, margin, procurement timing, conversion, or retention is evidenced, so the economic improvement remains unvalidated and no wealth outcome is claimed.

risks: No appointed controller or prime contractor may seek or select this supplier
The authority dependency remains real even though production is gated until the customer controls it
A prime contractor or public sponsor could internalize, retender, or replace the module and retain the institutional moat
Sensitive status leakage, false matches, missed matches, or weak appeals could materially harm participants
Long procurement and subcontractor sales cycles may still exceed the founder's preferred social and part-time operating model
Jurisdiction-specific law, integrations, and assurance may prevent the expected technical reuse
Milestone funding may not cover insurance, audits, uptime, incident response, and specialist support once production begins

structure.commercial_archetype: Authority-gated white-label infrastructure subcontractor with milestone-funded implementation and recurring operations
structure.control_point: A reusable technical module and operator-integration layer embedded in a sponsor-appointed controller's or prime contractor's authorized deployment; the founder company does not claim the public mandate
structure.critical_dependency: A sponsor-appointed controller or prime contractor must first pay for scoped discovery and prove lawful authority plus binding participant commitments before production work; no such buyer, authority, payment, or commitment is currently evidenced

thesis: Rather than attempting to create or own a Polish mandate, supply a reusable, jurisdiction-configurable self-exclusion status engine and operating toolkit to a sponsor-appointed independent controller or regulated-market prime contractor. The controller or prime owns the lawful basis, scheme rules, public authority, coalition work, and operator participation; the founder company supplies the minimized yes/no API, adapter kit, audit and appeals tooling, and contracted technical operations. Production work begins only after a paid scoped technical-discovery milestone and documentary evidence that the customer controls the governance mandate and binding participant commitments. The reviewed foreign schemes support compulsory coverage and technical feasibility, not demand for this supplier, outsourcing, or Polish procurement. This redesign therefore gates rather than assumes the missing institutional control point and seeks reuse across authorized deployments.
title: Authority-Gated White-Label Self-Exclusion Infrastructure
uncertainties: Whether any sponsor-appointed controller or regulated-market prime seeks an external white-label technical supplier
Whether a paid technical-discovery engagement can precede scheme authorization under the relevant procurement route
Lawful basis, controller roles, data-category treatment, withdrawal mechanics, appeals, and liability allocation for any deployment
Whether a customer can secure binding operator participation and fund implementation without transferring the public mandate to the founder company
Identity matching, security certification, uptime, incident-response cost, prime-contractor economics, and founder support burden
Cross-jurisdiction reuse, procurement timing, supplier retention, and founder-net-worth timing
